title: School therapy staffing: buyer, provider and workflow evidence
scope: School-based therapist staffing, with SLP as the worked example and OT/PT comparisons where documented. The user changed the target from local healthcare to schools and therapists; the historical filename is retained only for build compatibility.
jurisdiction: Unselected. District examples are research evidence, not the pilot's adopted rules.
status: Public-source requirements candidates; no customer interviews, private-system access, procurement submissions, provider outreach or live student data used.
key_design_findings: Track clinician work time, student service delivery, and customer billable units separately.
The district may require its own timekeeping, student-record and teletherapy systems. A new vendor portal is not necessarily the system of record.
Provider credentials, assistant eligibility, delivery modality, calendar, billing and missed-service handling require district-specific rule versions.
AI can prepare, reconcile and flag administrative work. The district and qualified professionals retain service eligibility, IEP, assessment, treatment and clinical signoff decisions.
Public solicitations reveal useful requirements but do not prove an award, current Amergis execution, customer demand available to us or permission to access student records.

sources.title: Rockford Public Schools District 205 / Amergis professional services agreement and school staffing SOW
sources.published_or_effective: Agreement dated 2025-06-18; initial services term 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30; exercised renewal not established.
sources.section_or_page: PDF p10 §5(h); p16 §9(b)–(d); p32 Attachment A §5; p34 Attachment B §§1–2; pp7–8 §4(h)
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; actual preserved local PDF text independently checked.
sources.directly_observed_fact: The SOW lists OT/PT and assistant/SLP qualification levels. MaxView hours require weekly district approval. Invoices are weekly; verified payment follows Board approval. Per-diem cancellation and travel replacement clauses are distinct.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Historical district-specific contract evidence, not confirmed current operations. Role listing does not establish that every assistant can replace a therapist. Special per-diem/travel clauses do not establish ordinary term-assigned therapist closure rules.

sources.title: Knox County contract 25-287(b), RFP 3635, addenda and Amergis response
sources.published_or_effective: Packet published for 2025-06-04 agenda; initial term 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. Renewal unverified.
sources.section_or_page: PDF p19 §4.2.2; p21 §4.3; p37 Addendum I Q8; p38 Q17; p46 Addendum II Q7–12; p99 supplier clarification dated 2025-04-22
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; actual preserved local PDF text independently checked.
sources.directly_observed_fact: Knox rejects licensed therapy assistants, requires its timekeeping and supervisor approval, prefers email, and declines a VMS. The supplier says student data stays in district systems. SLP work includes service documentation and meetings.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Separate customer requirements from supplier statements. Initial term has ended. The SLP section contains apparent template errors and ambiguous billing terminology; preserve them for clarification.

sources.title: Bristol Virginia Public Schools RFP CO-04-202526: Occupational, Physical and Speech Therapy Services
sources.published_or_effective: Issued 2026-05-04; proposal deadline 2026-05-22. Award not investigated.
sources.section_or_page: PDF pp5–7, §5 Scope, §5.1 Progress Reports, §5.2 Missed Sessions, §5.3 Billing and §6 Payment
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 23 pages.
sources.directly_observed_fact: The IEP committee determines service eligibility, frequency and time. Teletherapy is excluded. Therapist absences are rescheduled; student absences reported monthly. Billing uses 15-minute units with specified inclusions and service detail. Historical caseload figures are not guaranteed volume.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: One district's solicitation, not an Amergis contract or nationwide rule. Medicaid-support wording is customer-specific and does not establish our own payer enrollment or claim authority.

sources.title: DCPS GAGA-2026-I-0191: School-Based Related Services solicitation
sources.published_or_effective: Issued 2026-06-23; bids due 2026-07-06. Award and option exercise not established.
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 64 pages. Read alongside LC05 amendment and LC06 incorporated guidance.
sources.directly_observed_fact: The procurement covers leave replacement for OT/PT/SLP and excludes assistants. It specifies authorized orders, district documentation systems, school-day billing limits, nonbillable closures, documented service thresholds, missed-service plans and monthly electronic invoicing. Documentation thresholds and deadline wording differ across sections.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: District-specific IFB, not recovered Amergis operations. Several clauses use OT/PT-specific wording inside a broader related-services procurement. Resolve scope and conflicting text before implementation.

sources.title: DCPS GAGA-2026-I-0191 Amendment 001, questions and answers
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 4 pages.
sources.directly_observed_fact: DCPS seeks one vendor offering all requested disciplines. Virtual-only bids may be considered, with in-person preferred; virtual delivery must use DCPS's platform. Virtual staff retain specified attendance and screening requirements. Additional fees beyond the proposed hourly rate are excluded.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: This amendment modifies one procurement. It contradicts any assumption that a vendor can always use its own teletherapy platform or waive onsite-style screening for remote providers.

sources.title: DCPS Missed Related Services and Untimely Assessment Guidelines
sources.published_or_effective: Cover April 2017; page footers March 2017. Referenced and attached to the June 2026 procurement.
sources.retrieval: Fresh public PDF retrieval succeeded; 16 pages; official 2026 procurement links this document.
sources.directly_observed_fact: Guidance distinguishes provider absence, student absence/unavailability and school closure. Service and make-up records include reasons, durations, attempts and related communications. It uses legacy SEDS terminology, while the 2026 solicitation uses PSSP.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Do not apply a 2017 district procedure universally or translate its system names mechanically. District/clinician decisions about individual impact and remediation remain necessary.

sources.title: ASHA school services FAQ: caseload, workload, service delivery and work setting
sources.section_or_page: Questions: Does ASHA have a recommendation for caseload size?; policy on making up missed sessions?; one service delivery model versus another?
sources.retrieval: Fresh primary association webpage retrieval succeeded.
sources.directly_observed_fact: ASHA does not set a universal minimum/maximum caseload or a missed-session policy. It emphasizes total workload and individualized district consideration of missed-service impact. It does not prescribe a single service-delivery model.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Professional association guidance, not a substitute for selected-jurisdiction law, adopted district policy or a clinician's assessment.

sources.title: Amergis Educational Staffing Teletherapy Platform
sources.section_or_page: Security and accessibility; Clinically valid evaluations; Frequently Asked Questions
sources.directly_observed_fact: Amergis advertises room links without student accounts/downloads, waiting rooms, therapy-minute tracking, session-activity reporting and technical support. It also claims no stored student session data.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: Marketing capabilities and compliance claims are not independently verified architecture, APIs, permissions or certifications. Reporting versus no-storage scope remains unresolved. Do not infer licensed assessment reuse rights.

sources.title: Amergis school SLP posting, Willard Missouri, position 1179375
sources.directly_observed_fact: This posting requires active assignment-state SLP licensure, describes CCC-SLP as preferred or state/contract dependent, and makes several health credentials conditional. It describes evaluation and documentation duties and employment-status-dependent benefits.
sources.applicability_and_limitations: One supplier job description, not authoritative Missouri law, a guaranteed vacancy, actual compensation or universal SLP qualification policy. URL job number and displayed position ID differ; retain both.

requirement_candidates.name: Authorized demand and district rule version
requirement_candidates.actor: District procurement/HR/SPED owner and staffing operations
requirement_candidates.trigger: New or changed therapy staffing request
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Bind the request to an authorized order, discipline, assignment dates, school sites, delivery mode, budget/rate approval and adopted rule-pack version. Record which district role can approve each field.
requirement_candidates.exception: Unapproved extension, expired order or contradictory source document routes to the named district owner.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic schedule extension without authorized funding remains pending; an existing valid order continues unaffected.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed order requirements; proposed data model and release gate.
requirement_candidates.title: Authorized demand and district rule version

requirement_candidates.name: Discipline and qualification-level eligibility
requirement_candidates.actor: Credential reviewer and district hiring authority
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Evaluate district × discipline × qualification-level requirements separately. Store verification evidence, applicability, expiry and reviewer. Keep SLP, SLP-CF, SLPA, OT/COTA and PT/PTA distinct.
requirement_candidates.exception: Assistant substitution or conditional credential with unresolved applicability requires review; document upload alone does not clear eligibility.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: The same synthetic SLPA is excluded from a district profile prohibiting assistants and reviewed under an explicit assistant-permitting profile, without changing the original SLP order.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed differing customer criteria; proposed eligibility implementation.
requirement_candidates.title: Discipline and qualification-level eligibility

requirement_candidates.name: District-controlled modality and delivery platform
requirement_candidates.actor: District SPED/IT owner and licensed provider
requirement_candidates.trigger: Selecting onsite, virtual or hybrid delivery
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Store approved modality, permitted platform, school facilitator/equipment prerequisites and change authority. The agent can check readiness and route a request; it cannot switch a student's service mode.
requirement_candidates.exception: Customer forbids teletherapy, requires its own platform or lacks access approval.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: Synthetic Bristol-profile demand cannot be fulfilled virtually; a DCPS-profile virtual assignment requires the district-designated platform.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed procurement differences; proposed enforcement and readiness checklist.
requirement_candidates.title: District-controlled modality and delivery platform

requirement_candidates.name: Separate service plan from staffing logistics
requirement_candidates.actor: District IEP team/qualified clinician; staffing scheduler
requirement_candidates.trigger: Approved service plan or caseload change
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Reference the district-approved service-plan version and necessary scheduling constraints. Record operational impacts separately from eligibility, goals, clinical findings and service-frequency decisions, which stay with authorized professionals.
requirement_candidates.exception: A requested schedule conflicts with the authorized service plan or no approved plan reference exists.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: An agent can propose available timetable slots but cannot alter a student's authorized minutes or mark a clinical decision approved.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed district authority and plan-linked delivery; proposed access boundaries.
requirement_candidates.title: Separate service plan from staffing logistics

requirement_candidates.name: Workload capacity beyond student count
requirement_candidates.actor: Clinical lead and district program manager
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Model direct services, consultation, evaluations, meetings, documentation, travel and supervision separately. Use provider-reviewed capacity assumptions and a feasible calendar; do not invent a universal maximum caseload.
requirement_candidates.exception: Available working time is insufficient even when student count appears low.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic request with acceptable headcount but excessive meetings/travel is flagged with the time deficit and routed to the clinical lead.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed workload guidance and procurement inclusions; proposed capacity model.
requirement_candidates.title: Workload capacity beyond student count

requirement_candidates.name: Three linked but distinct activity ledgers
requirement_candidates.actor: Therapist, time approver and billing specialist
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Maintain separate clinician work-time, student service/attempt evidence references and customer billing entries, linked through assignment and date. Reconcile them without treating each hour worked as delivered therapy or each session minute as separately billable.
requirement_candidates.exception: Meetings, documentation, group sessions or bundled costs produce legitimate differences between ledgers.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic day containing therapy, an IEP meeting and documentation produces correct distinct totals with no duplicate charge.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed distinct documentation and commercial measures; proposed ledger design.
requirement_candidates.title: Three linked but distinct activity ledgers

requirement_candidates.name: District student-record ownership and controlled references
requirement_candidates.actor: District records/IT owner, provider and integration operator
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Identify the authoritative student-record system, permitted access, required document states and allowed administrative evidence. Prefer minimal references/completion attestations when full records are unnecessary. Map legacy terminology only after district confirmation.
requirement_candidates.exception: A district API/export is unavailable, permission is missing or imported identifiers do not reconcile.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: The synthetic workflow can prove documentation completion using approved reference IDs without copying clinical narrative into the staffing CRM.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed district-system requirements; proposed minimization and adapter contract.
requirement_candidates.title: District student-record ownership and controlled references

requirement_candidates.name: Missed-session cause and disposition
requirement_candidates.actor: Provider, district case manager and program manager
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Record a specific cause, planned versus delivered duration, attempted delivery and supporting communication. Route clinical impact, due diligence and remedy decisions to the designated professional; track approved recovery rather than assume every absence is identical.
requirement_candidates.exception: Provider absence, student absence, student unavailability, school closure and technical failure have different adopted handling.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: Synthetic provider illness and school closure create different routed cases under their approved district rule version, with no automatic clinical determination.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed reason-specific guidance; proposed case workflow.
requirement_candidates.title: Missed-session cause and disposition

requirement_candidates.name: Planned absence and provider transition continuity
requirement_candidates.actor: Staffing coordinator, clinical supervisor and district approver
requirement_candidates.trigger: Leave, resignation, delayed start or uncovered assignment
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Identify affected scheduled services, prepare a coverage/handoff proposal, obtain required district approvals and retain replacement readiness and notification evidence. Link missed services to later recovery records.
requirement_candidates.exception: Replacement lacks credentials, approved access or available capacity; a deadline cannot be met.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: An announced absence surfaces affected synthetic commitments and cannot be marked resolved merely because a replacement candidate was contacted.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed missed-service-plan requirements; proposed operational tracking.
requirement_candidates.title: Planned absence and provider transition continuity

requirement_candidates.name: School calendars and commercial treatment
requirement_candidates.actor: District calendar owner and staffing finance
requirement_candidates.trigger: Holiday, delayed opening, closure, ESY or assignment change
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Version the district calendar and distinguish closure, scheduled break, absence and contract cancellation. Apply only adopted assignment-specific commercial rules; evaluate worker-pay obligations separately.
requirement_candidates.exception: A per-diem cancellation clause is proposed for a term assignment or ESY falls outside purchased scope.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic term-assigned SLP closure cannot inherit a per-diem two-hour cancellation fee without an applicable rule and approval.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed clause scope differences; proposed category guards.
requirement_candidates.title: School calendars and commercial treatment

requirement_candidates.name: Client-controlled time approval channel
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Accept the agreed source and approval channel, including district systems or approved imports. Retain approver, version, actual approval time and corrections; configure local deadline semantics and extension authority.
requirement_candidates.exception: No approval, disputed hours, timezone ambiguity or corrected source timecard.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: Two synthetic clients use different approval channels while preserving the same audit fields; a correction does not overwrite the approved original.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed MaxView versus district-timekeeping contrast; proposed common record model.
requirement_candidates.title: Client-controlled time approval channel

requirement_candidates.name: Configurable invoice units, inclusions and approval events
requirement_candidates.actor: Billing specialist and district finance approver
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Resolve rate, unit basis, bundled inclusions, separately authorized extras, cadence and payment trigger from the signed rule pack. Keep customer approval, invoice submission and cash receipt as separate events.
requirement_candidates.exception: Included meeting/travel cost is charged twice or a payment clock starts from the wrong approval event.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic unit-based contract and an inclusive hourly contract produce different correct invoices; no additional fee appears where the profile excludes it.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed contrasting commercial structures; proposed rules engine and reconciliation.
requirement_candidates.title: Configurable invoice units, inclusions and approval events

requirement_candidates.name: Documentation readiness and unresolved rule conflicts
requirement_candidates.actor: District contract owner, documentation reviewer and billing specialist
requirement_candidates.trigger: Adopting a rule pack or releasing a customer invoice
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Represent required documentation and verification gates explicitly. When source sections conflict, preserve both with citations and request a written governing interpretation before enabling the affected automated rule. Invoice readiness must not silently decide worker-pay eligibility.
requirement_candidates.exception: Different percentage/deadline wording, apparent copied role labels, or obsolete system names.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: The DCPS fixture remains unresolved until an approver chooses and records the governing threshold/deadline; the agent cannot silently select the easier clause.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed source ambiguities; proposed fail-safe adoption process.
requirement_candidates.title: Documentation readiness and unresolved rule conflicts

requirement_candidates.name: Virtual-session operational evidence and technical recovery
requirement_candidates.actor: Provider, district facilitator/IT and support operator
requirement_candidates.trigger: Approved virtual session setup or connection failure
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Verify approved platform access, device readiness and support ownership. Record operational session status separately from provider-signed clinical notes; route outages and incomplete sessions into the district-approved exception process.
requirement_candidates.exception: A room link, attendance event or vendor activity report is mistaken for proof of delivered clinical service.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic connected-but-interrupted session cannot be auto-certified as completed therapy; reporting and retention responsibilities are documented before any live deployment.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed advertised tools and district platform requirement; proposed validation requirements.
requirement_candidates.title: Virtual-session operational evidence and technical recovery

requirement_candidates.name: Role-specific onboarding and continuing readiness
requirement_candidates.actor: Credential owner, district onboarding contact and clinical supervisor
requirement_candidates.trigger: Prestart, credential expiration, changed location/modality or renewal
requirement_candidates.required_behavior: Track state/profession checks, district screening, required orientation, documentation-system access and supervision arrangements as separate readiness items. Reassess changed assignments and preserve the authority behind any exception.
requirement_candidates.exception: Remote status is incorrectly treated as a blanket waiver or a generic SLP posting is substituted for district requirements.
requirement_candidates.acceptance: A synthetic remote provider missing a district-required item stays pending even with a complete resume and active professional license.
requirement_candidates.confidence: Observed conditional and customer-specific screening; proposed readiness implementation.
requirement_candidates.title: Role-specific onboarding and continuing readiness

source_exceptions.issue: PDF p19 SLP subsection labels one face-to-face-time bullet School Psychologists and uses Medicare terminology.
source_exceptions.treatment: Preserve the literal text; obtain the district's intended role and billing-system interpretation. Do not silently rewrite to Medicaid.

source_exceptions.issue: Typical workday wording and the addendum's no-minimum-service-hours answer describe different concepts.
source_exceptions.treatment: Separate standard schedule, authorized quantity and guaranteed billable volume.

source_exceptions.issue: §C.5.31 describes 95% documentation, while §C.8.1.4 says confirm 100%; the performance table also uses a different Monday deadline and cross-references.
source_exceptions.treatment: Do not assume a single operative threshold or deadline until the district contract owner resolves their scopes.

source_exceptions.issue: The incorporated 2017 guidance uses SEDS; the 2026 procurement uses PSSP and Frontline.
source_exceptions.treatment: Confirm current systems, exact field mapping and continued procedural applicability; do not recreate a retired interface.

source_exceptions.issue: No stored student session data is advertised alongside session-activity reports and minute tracking.
source_exceptions.treatment: Require a concrete retention/data-flow explanation before selecting or integrating any equivalent vendor.

source_exceptions.issue: Published initial contract terms ended June 30, 2026 and current renewal/execution status is unverified.
source_exceptions.treatment: Use as historical configuration examples, not active requirements of the pilot.

remaining_discovery_questions: Which state, school district type and initial discipline are in scope: SLP only, or a bundled SLP/OT/PT service?
Are we supplying staff under district direction, contracting to deliver defined therapy services, or both? Who retains service-record and clinical-supervision responsibility?
Which roles approve requisitions, budgets, candidates, onboarding, schedules, documentation, time and invoices? Obtain the current signed agreement, SOW, amendments and order form.
Which existing district systems own student records, service schedules, therapist attendance, Medicaid support and accounts payable? What permitted API, export or manual evidence channels exist?
What direct/indirect workload, travel, meetings and supervision must fit into each provider's contracted time? What constitutes an accepted workload change?
How do provider absence, student absence, school closure, testing schedules, technology failure and planned leave each affect service recovery, customer billing and worker pay?
Who decides whether missed services require recovery, which plan is approved and when an exception can be closed?
Are assistants and clinical fellows permitted, under what supervision, and can a replacement change qualification level?
When is virtual delivery allowed, who chooses the platform, and what school-side facilitator, room, device and accessibility support is required?
Which student-linked data are actually necessary in the staffing system, who may see them, and what approved retention/deletion rules apply?
How are invoice disputes, after-submission corrections and actual cash receipt measured? What is the complete payment trigger, not just the stated number of days?
Which three recurring exceptions consume the most staff time, and what evidence would let an agent safely prepare the next action?

interview_guides.audience: District special-education director or therapy program lead, with HR/procurement and finance represented
interview_guides.format: Proposed 45–60 minute walkthrough using synthetic or fully de-identified examples; no outreach performed.
questions: Walk through the last therapist vacancy from need identification to first completed service. Where did it wait and why?
Show the blank forms and approval chain for a new order, candidate, schedule and assignment extension.
Which services and administrative duties are included in the requested hours, and who checks that the workload fits?
Which systems must a supplier use? Where do staff currently re-enter the same information?
Walk through one provider absence, one student absence and one closure. Who makes the recovery and billing decisions?
What evidence makes a timecard and invoice acceptable? What causes rejection or delayed payment?
Which actions could a staffing agent execute under a preapproved rule, and which require a named person's decision?
artifacts_to_request: De-identified exception categories and timing counts

interview_guides.audience: School SLP, plus OT/PT comparison participants if those disciplines enter scope
interview_guides.format: Proposed 45 minute day-in-the-life walkthrough; no student identities or clinical narratives collected.
questions: Map a normal week across direct service, evaluation, documentation, meetings, consultation and travel.
What information must you receive before accepting an assignment? Which surprises make an assignment unworkable?
Where do you record work time versus service delivery? What gets entered twice?
What happens when a session is missed or only partly delivered? Which decisions require your judgment?
Which reminders, prefilled administrative forms or reconciliation checks would save time without creating extra review?
How do you obtain support for access problems, room/equipment issues, workload changes and payroll corrections?
For virtual work, what happens at the school end before a session can start, and how are outages recorded?

interview_guides.audience: Recruiter/account manager, credential specialist, clinical supervisor and time/billing operator
interview_guides.format: Proposed 60 minute end-to-end tabletop using one synthetic SLP placement; no outreach performed.
questions: Which candidate and client facts must be verified rather than inferred before submission or start?
Where are district-specific rules stored, who updates them, and how do amendments reach payroll and billing?
What handoff makes a selected candidate ready to start? What is still unresolved after the client says yes?
How do you replace a provider while preserving access, qualification, supervision and continuity requirements?
How do time, documentation and invoice exceptions get reconciled without delaying unrelated obligations?
What cannot currently be observed through APIs or exports, and who can authorize an approved integration?
Show the evidence needed to reverse an incorrect agent action and identify who owns the recovery.
artifacts_to_request: Approval and escalation roster by role

research_limits: No jurisdiction or real district is selected; numerical clauses are examples rather than adopted pilot defaults.
No interviews were conducted, so frequency, pain severity, current practices and willingness to use a new portal remain hypotheses.
This research does not determine student service eligibility, clinical treatment, IEP content, employment classification or legal compliance.
No full proprietary assessment instruments, private portals, personal student records or authenticated tenant data were extracted.
